title: ChartBook lockfile
description: The file `chartbook pin` writes as chartbook.lock: the exact bytes a pipeline depends on. It has the index's envelope without `generated_at` and `generator`, so that pinning twice with nothing changed writes the same file. Its records are the index's records with fields left out: the pipeline's own record, cut down to its dependencies, and one record for each asset of each dependency that code reads. Version 2 holds a dataframe and a model always, and a chart, a notebook, a note or a file only when its owner's manifest says `lock = true` (the record then has `lock`); version 1 held a record for every asset. An asset that is not in it is read from the snapshot its dependency's entry names.

root.description: The ID of the pipeline the lockfile belongs to.

records.description: First the pipeline's own record, then one record per asset of each dependency that the lockfile holds, sorted by ID. A labelled version of a dependency's model is a record of its own, `dep:model/x@champion`, with `ref.rev` and `label` set and the version's `content_hash`; one without a `content_hash` has `missing`, why the store could not supply it. An asset record with a `content_hash` is a pin; one without is declared by the other pipeline and was not built when this was pinned.

dependencies.description: On the Pipeline record: each dependency as in the index's Pipeline record, by its key in [dependencies], with no absolute path. `pinned_hash` is one hash over everything pinned of it, labelled versions included; a dependency none of whose assets is in the lockfile has none. A dependency pinned from a snapshot has the snapshot's commit in `location.commit` and its time in `snapshot`, which is the whole of its pin when none of its assets is in the lockfile, and where an asset that is not in the lockfile is read from. `pinned_from` is the pipeline the pins came from, by its own ID rather than the key: the snapshot's pipeline, or the one a `git` dependency's clone holds; a pin made before 0.3.0 has none until it is made again or moved.

date_col.description: On a dataframe: the column its rows are dated by, as its entry declares it, when its rows are hashed by period.

as_of.description: The last timestamp in the dataframe's date column when its rows were hashed: the data's own last date, never the time on the clock. In UTC, a date alone at midnight (`2026-10-30`), else with its time (`2026-10-30T16:00:00`, with a fraction of six or nine digits where it has one). Absent for a dataframe with no date column, or with no dated row.

rows.description: The rows hash of each period of the dataframe (`chartbook.rowhash`; the form is in the index specification, "The rows hash"), by the period: the first and the last timestamp seen in it, both included, written as `as_of` is and joined by `/` (`1961-06-14/1961-12-29`). `none` is the period of the rows with no date. A dataframe with no date column has one entry, `all`. Whoever checks a pin hashes their own rows in these same periods, leaving out the rows after `as_of`.

not_hashed.description: Why the dataframe's rows have no hash, where they have none: a column of a kind the form does not take, a piece too large to hold, more columns than are read at once. A pin of it is then met by the same file only. Absent when `rows` is there.

row_count.description: On a dataframe whose rows are hashed: how many rows it has.

lock.description: The asset's owner marks it `lock = true`, which is why a chart, a notebook, a note or a file is in the lockfile. Present only when it does.
